Emily Chen: heads up — our pass@k numbers on the new quantized t5-3b rollout look... wrong. reported 0.72 for k=5 but local re-runs give ~0.58. anyone else seeing inflation?
Marc Rivera: hmm that's a big delta. starting point: are we deduping samples before computing pass@k?
Emily Chen: i checked the runner, it just appends candidate outputs and counts unique==gold. i think we forgot to dedupe identical candidates across sampled seeds. simple repro attached below.
Devon Patel: can you paste the compute snippet? i can run a quick diff with the old harness.
Emily Chen: ```python
# current naive pass@k impl
def pass_at_k(candidates, gold, k):
    # candidates: list of strings (may include duplicates)
    hits = 0
    for i in range(0, len(candidates), k):
        batch = candidates[i:i+k]
        if gold in batch:
            hits += 1
    return hits / (len(candidates) / k)
```
Olga Sokolov: ohhhh — that slices by raw candidates length. if the sampling produced duplicate strings across seeds, those count toward more buckets. pass@k is supposed to sample k unique candidates per example (see original paper).
Marc Rivera: exactly. we need to apply deduplication per-example before computing buckets. something like: `uniq = list(dict.fromkeys(candidates))` or use set but preserve order.
Devon Patel: another gotcha: our CI tests use a tiny seed pool (n=20 with heavy quant noise) so dupes are common. fluffing dupes inflates pass@k because duplicate bad answers can push gold into a different bucket less frequently? it's subtle but explains the 0.72.
Emily Chen: ran a quick patch locally: dedupe then compute -> pass@5 becomes 0.59. patch diff in thread.
Marc Rivera: great. can we also add a unit test that constructs repeated identical candidates and verifies stable pass@k? i can add to eval-runner/tests/test_metrics.py.
Olga Sokolov: yes and add a test where n < k to match edge case (should return 1 if gold in uniq set? need to follow the definition we agreed on). document the contract.
Emily Chen: note: while we're here, we should standardize tokenization for BLEU/ROUGE. i found the harness using sacrebleu tokenization in one path but plain whitespace split in another — causes small BLEU deltas across runs.
Devon Patel: ugh. which codepaths?
Emily Chen: metrics/bleu.py calls sacrebleu.corpus_bleu(tokens, tokenize='13a') but our legacy eval runner calls nltk.word_tokenize then joins. we should centralize to a single util and surface the tokenizer choice in the CI summary.
Marc Rivera: also BERTScore — huggingface version changed scorer defaults (rescale_with_baseline toggled). saw a bump in bertscore on the new model vs baseline that disappeared when rescale_with_baseline=False. need to pin library versions or set explicit kwargs.
Olga Sokolov: +1 pinning. please add the exact package versions to eval_env/requirements.txt and the metric wrappers should accept explicit kwargs.
Emily Chen: action items: 1) Marc to PR dedupe fix + unit tests (will include edgecases). 2) Devon to centralize tokenizer util and migrate BLEU/ROUGE callers. 3) Olga to pin bertscore/sacrebleu versions and add CI smoke comparing pinned vs latest. i'll open issues and link PRs.
Marc Rivera: i'll target a small patch: eval-runner#452. tests: construct a candidates list with repeats and assert pass@k computed on deduped list. also add a quick perf microbenchmark to ensure we don't regress large-n path.
Devon Patel: i'll do tokenizer PR eval-runner#453, add contract doc in docs/eval_metrics.md explaining tokenization choices for each metric.
Olga Sokolov: i'm on bertscore pin and a CI job that runs metrics on a fixed prompt set (deterministic seeds + quant determinism flag). eval-bot, can you schedule a nightly job to run the pinned-metrics smoke?
eval-bot: scheduled nightly run "eval-metrics-smoke-pinned" at 03:15 UTC. job id: ems-202-2023.
Emily Chen: thanks. one more note: add a small entry in the release notes about pass@k contract change — any downstream dashboards that ingest pass@k numbers (product/bench) need to be aware of dedupe semantics, otherwise comparisons across historical runs will be apples-to-oranges.
Marc Rivera: good catch. i'll ping product/bench once PR merges.
Devon Patel: TL;DR: bug was double-counting due to duplicates in candidate sampling; fixes: dedupe before bucketing, pin tokenizer/metric versions, add unit tests + CI smoke, and update docs/release notes.
Olga Sokolov: moving to a follow-up thread for dashboard migration. thanks everyone :tada:
